purpose: Determine whether the frozen experiment matrix, preregistration, target chain and failure tree define one reproducible confirmatory analysis capable of supporting a bounded SCI claim. This audit does not amend the frozen plan, inspect outcomes, execute an optimizer/evaluator or consume formal FFE.

input: accepted frozen plan and immutable snapshot identity
live plan, preregistration, experiment matrix, target chain, failure tree, plan specification and reproducibility checklist
pending M/H precedence amendment and five independent unresolved author gates
zero formal run and zero formal FFE scientific state
output: multiplicity, missingness and exact-test gap map
analysis_contract.process: bind live bytes and prior authority -> compare estimand to operational endpoint -> trace run/seed/problem aggregation -> audit exact-test and multiplicity contracts -> audit failure/missingness actions -> classify evidence consequences
analysis_contract.flow_logic: frozen plan -> immutable run schema -> run-level measurement -> seed-level aggregation -> problem-level effect -> cross-problem inference -> multiplicity-controlled branch -> allowed claim

pending_M_H_amendment.audit_treatment: The author-selected 2,000D M budget and fixed-checkpoint H1 endpoint are treated as pending precedence choices, not as frozen authority. This audit does not reopen or freeze them.

structural_gate_context.research_package_final: not released; historical manifest has handoff authorization gaps
structural_gate_context.interpretation: These gates verify declared structure. They do not prove that seed aggregation, A12 estimation, exact zero/tie inference, cross-hypothesis multiplicity or unresolved-run handling has one mathematical implementation.

findings.title: H1 and H2 do not define the unique path from 30 seed runs to one problem-level endpoint
evidence: preregistration_candidate_v0.1.md:55 declares 30 runs per problem and seed is not the inferential unit
preregistration_candidate_v0.1.md:72 defines a four-checkpoint median NMI but does not state whether checkpoints are aggregated before or after the 30 seeds

preregistration_candidate_v0.1.md:76 defines a problem-level directional-success proportion but does not state whether donor events are pooled across runs, run proportions are equally weighted, or seed-paired contrasts are aggregated
.light/target_chain_I3_CVGR_v0.1.json declares problem as the analysis unit but leaves the within-problem seed estimator implicit
findings.why_it_changes_results: Median-over-checkpoints then median-over-seeds, median-over-seeds then median-over-checkpoints, and pooling all events are not algebraically equivalent. Event pooling additionally weights long or frequently activating runs more heavily.
findings.required_resolution: Freeze a two-stage estimator for each endpoint, including run-level numerator/denominator, inactive-run handling, seed-paired contrast, problem aggregation and the exploratory status of any event-weighted alternative.

findings.title: H3 uses common random numbers but does not uniquely define the A12 estimand or estimator
evidence: PROJECT_PLAN.md:78 states that algorithms use the same 30 seeds
preregistration_candidate_v0.1.md:80 says A12 is estimated from 30 outputs per algorithm

.light/target_chain_I3_CVGR_v0.1.json operationally mentions 30 outcomes but does not state whether A12 uses all 900 cross-algorithm pairs, only 30 aligned-seed pairs, or excludes the 30 correlated diagonal pairs
findings.why_it_changes_results: All-pairs Vargha-Delaney A12 and aligned-seed superiority probability estimate different quantities. Under common random numbers, the diagonal pairs are dependent and cannot be silently treated as ordinary independent two-sample pairs.
findings.required_resolution: Freeze the exact comparison kernel, tie weight, pair set and estimator name. If conventional all-pairs A12 is retained, predefine a CRN-aware paired sensitivity analysis and uncertainty method; if aligned pairs are primary, rename the endpoint and revisit the 0.56 threshold.

findings.title: The promised exact Wilcoxon analysis is not executable under the natural zero and tie patterns
evidence: PROJECT_PLAN.md:117 specifies one-sided exact Wilcoxon tests
PROJECT_PLAN.md:119 defers zero-difference and tie handling to a future frozen library implementation
reproducibility-checklist.md:53 leaves Holm family, zero/tie handling and A12 direction unchecked
H1/H2 assign zero to inactive problems and H3 uses discrete A12 values, so zero differences and tied absolute ranks are expected rather than exceptional
findings.why_it_changes_results: Library versions differ in whether they use asymptotic or exact calculations and how they treat zero differences and tied ranks. The resulting p values and Holm branches can differ for the same immutable data.
findings.required_resolution: Freeze a library-independent enumerated signed-rank or alternative exact procedure, including zero method, midrank rule, alternative direction, p-value definition, all-zero action and test vectors with hand-computable expected values.

findings.title: Multiplicity is controlled within each hypothesis but not across the selectable H1/H2 mechanism route and H3 paper claim
evidence: PROJECT_PLAN.md:117 limits Holm correction to the comparisons within one hypothesis
PROJECT_PLAN.md:149 permits the paper route when H3 and at least one of H1 or H2 succeeds
preregistration_candidate_v0.1.md:96 requires H3 success with H1/H2 merely not failed, while the final paper gate later selects at least one successful mechanism hypothesis
findings.why_it_changes_results: Selecting whichever of H1 or H2 passes after separate within-hypothesis corrections inflates the chance of a mechanism-supported paper claim. The distinction between non-failure and positive support is also not resolved in the H3 branch.
findings.required_resolution: Freeze one global confirmatory claim family and gatekeeping rule. A defensible option is to form one intersection-union p value for each of H1, H2 and H3, then apply Holm across those three global hypotheses; H4 remains a deterministic integrity gate.

findings.title: The <=5 percent unresolved infrastructure-failure case and paired-seed handling are undefined
evidence: preregistration_candidate_v0.1.md:103-104 allows one same-seed recovery and marks a comparison missing only when failures exceed 5 percent
with 30 runs, one unresolved run is 3.33 percent and two are 6.67 percent, but the plan does not state what happens to the one unresolved run
the plan does not state whether the matched run from the other algorithm is retained, removed as a pair, or used in an unequal-sample estimator
findings.why_it_changes_results: Different complete-case and unequal-sample choices change H1/H2 seed contrasts and H3 A12. Deciding this after observing failures would be an outcome-dependent exclusion rule.
findings.required_resolution: Freeze the exact integer threshold, pair-complete rule, denominator, minimum analyzable runs, whole-hypothesis action and immutable retention of original plus retry packages before any formal execution.

findings.title: The independent-problem assumption and inferential population are stronger than the fixed benchmark construction supports
evidence: the 12 synthetic problems are a complete 3x2x2 deterministic factorial family rather than a random sample
the 16 CEC2006 problems are a fixed eligibility subset
target-chain analysis families call these problems independent generalization units
findings.consequence: Cross-problem p values can be read as superpopulation evidence even though the plan only has a fixed benchmark census and related task families.
findings.required_resolution: Define the finite benchmark population as the primary scope, state the exchangeability/symmetry assumption explicitly, report all task effects and factorial strata, and prohibit extrapolation beyond the frozen suites without a separately frozen modern-family analysis.

findings.title: Thirty seeds are fixed without a Monte Carlo precision target or uncertainty contract
evidence: PROJECT_PLAN.md:121 states that no conventional 80 percent power claim is made
the preregistration reports point effects and q values but does not define confidence intervals for seed-derived NMI, proportions or A12
the 0.56 A12 success boundary is close enough to 0.5 that within-problem Monte Carlo uncertainty can affect classification
findings.consequence: The plan avoids seed pseudo-replication but does not show what stochastic effect precision 30 runs can support.
findings.required_resolution: Predefine paired seed bootstrap or another CRN-aware interval, Monte Carlo standard error reporting and a fixed sensitivity analysis for n=30; do not use observed post hoc power.

findings.title: Algorithm-attributable failure is defined for final performance but not for H1/H2 mechanism endpoints
evidence: preregistration_candidate_v0.1.md:101 assigns a worst constraint-first final outcome to NaN, illegal index or internal exception
the same section does not define the NMI checkpoint series, activation count or directional-success denominator for a failed mechanism run
findings.consequence: A failed run could be excluded from H1/H2 while being penalized in H3, creating inconsistent evidence and survivorship bias.
findings.required_resolution: Freeze fail-closed H1/H2 run records and endpoint values for each algorithm failure code, distinct from infrastructure missingness.

findings.title: H4 alternates between 240 paired comparisons and 480 individual run traces
evidence: experiment_matrix.md:10 describes all 8x30 runs against the parent
.light/failure_tree_I3_CVGR_v0.1.json declares inconclusive when expected trace count is below 480
8 problems x 30 seeds yields 240 CVGR-parent pairs but 480 individual algorithm traces
findings.consequence: A report can reach 100 percent using different denominators while still appearing compliant.
findings.required_resolution: Freeze both expected counts: 480 immutable run packages forming exactly 240 pair keys, and require zero missing packages, zero missing pairs and zero mismatches.

findings.title: Primary SESOI thresholds are decision values without a predeclared robustness envelope
evidence: PROJECT_PLAN.md:83 says A12=0.56 is preregistered but not a literature-established domain constant
.light/plan_spec_I3_CVGR_v0.1.json states that no credible prior problem-level effect distribution exists
NMI=0.60, delta-NMI=0.20 and direction-delta=0.05 likewise have no recorded external or pilot source
findings.consequence: The thresholds are valid decision rules but cannot be presented as established scientific importance boundaries.
findings.required_resolution: Label them project decision thresholds, preserve them for confirmatory branching, and predeclare threshold-sensitivity plots as secondary without using them to rescue a failed primary branch.

findings.title: The 25 percent wall-clock guardrail lacks an operational estimator
evidence: PROJECT_PLAN.md:143 and the failure tree use a median overhead threshold of 25 percent
ROB-02 specifies hardware, single-thread and warm-up but not timer boundaries, paired ratio, aggregation order, repetition count or handling of near-zero parent times
findings.consequence: The same timing records can produce different guardrail decisions and efficiency claims.
findings.required_resolution: Freeze timer scope, warm-up exclusion, paired seed/problem ratio, robust aggregation order, clock source, process isolation and a no-efficiency-claim action for unstable timing.

nonoverlap_with_existing_pending_gates: M/H candidate governs only the selected 2,000D budget and fixed-checkpoint H1 timing
parent-identity candidate governs the citable SHADE/Deb composite and parent conformance
modern-benchmark candidate governs benchmark and external-baseline identity, license and FFE adapters
novelty-control candidate governs Ray-style collision control and narrowed originality claims
mechanism-integrity candidate governs graph mathematics, donor semantics, FFE attempts, cache and path identity
this audit governs the run-to-seed-to-problem estimators, exact inference, global multiplicity and failure/missingness analysis contract

verdict.rationale: Five critical analysis choices can change primary endpoints, p values or branch decisions for the same immutable run packages. They must be fixed before result access and before an analysis script is allowed to consume formal data.

governance_effect.next_gate: Author decision on preparation of a versioned statistical-analysis amendment and additive static/expected-red analysis-contract tests only.
required_sequence: author selects the critical statistical semantics
prepare additive amendment, machine analysis specification and hand-computable red fixtures
separately freeze and restore that amendment
only then authorize analysis implementation and green tests
optimizer/evaluator execution remains behind later independent gates

actions_not_taken: No frozen plan, snapshot, source, test or analysis artifact was edited.
No statistical choice was silently selected for the author.
No optimizer, benchmark, evaluator, objective or constraint function was called.
No formal run package or formal FFE was created.
No performance, superiority, novelty, convergence, robustness or paper-readiness conclusion was formed.
